parsed_record.title: The antichain trace conjecture
parsed_record.statement:
Let $[n]=\{1,2,\ldots,n\}$, let $2^{[n]}$ be its powerset, and for a family $\mathcal{F}\subset 2^{[n]}$ and $Y\subset[n]$ write $\mathcal{F}_{\mid Y}=\{F\cap Y:F\in\mathcal{F}\}$. An **antichain** is a family in which no distinct members contain one another. The notation $\mathcal{F}\not\rightarrow(k+1,2^{k+1})$ means that no $(k+1)$-element subset $Y\subset[n]$ has $|\mathcal{F}_{\mid Y}|\geq 2^{k+1}$.

**The antichain trace conjecture.** Let $k$ be a non-negative integer and let $n\geq 2k$. If $\mathcal{F}\subset 2^{[n]}$ is an antichain satisfying $\mathcal{F}\not\rightarrow(k+1,2^{k+1})$, then

$$
|\mathcal{F}|\leq \binom{n}{k}.
$$

This is presented as an old conjecture. The surrounding results relate trace conditions for down-sets to forbidden complete uniform hypergraphs, but do not resolve this antichain bound.
parsed_record.source_name: Peter Frankl and Jian Wang, “Four-vertex traces of finite sets”, arXiv:2301.05830 (2023).
parsed_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.05830

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2023).

parsed_record.title: The graph-isomorphism conjecture for rational quadratic-form graphs
parsed_record.statement:
Let $q_1,q_2\boxtimes$ be quadratic forms on $\operatorname{\mathbb{Q}}^n$, and let $G_0(\operatorname{\mathbb{Q}}^n,q)$ denote the connected component containing $\operatorname{\textbf{0}}$ in $G(\operatorname{\mathbb{Q}}^n,q)$. Write $q_1\stackrel{\operatorname{\mathbb{Q}}}{\sim}q_2$ when the forms are rationally equivalent. **Graph-isomorphism conjecture.** If $G_0(\operatorname{\mathbb{Q}}^n,q_1)\simeq G_0(\operatorname{\mathbb{Q}}^n,q_2)$, then $q_1\stackrel{\operatorname{\mathbb{Q}}}{\sim}q_2$. Moreover, every isomorphism between these graphs is a linear transformation $T$ such that

$$
q_1(\operatorname{\textbf{x}})=q_2(T\operatorname{\textbf{x}}).
$$

This conjecture generalises the rational Beckman--Quarles theorem: when $q_1=q_2=I_n$, it asserts that every automorphism of $G_0(\operatorname{\mathbb{Q}}^n,I_n)$ is an isometry.
parsed_record.source_name: Artemy Sokolov, “On distance graphs in rational spaces”, arXiv:2301.06954 (2023).
parsed_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.06954

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2023).

parsed_record.title: Frankl–Kupavskii stability conjecture for bounded matching number
parsed_record.statement:
Let $n,k,t$ be positive integers with $n>kt$. Let $F$ be a $k$-graph of order $n$. For a hypergraph $F$, write $
u(F)$ for its matching number, $\tau(F)$ for its vertex-cover number, and $e(F)$ for its number of edges. For $i\in [k]$, let

$$
{\cal A}_i^{(k)}(n,t)=\left\\{A\in {[n]\choose k}: \left|A\cap [(t+1)i-1]\right|\ge i\right\\},
$$

and let

$$
{\cal H}^{(k)}(n,t)=\left\\{e\in {[n]\choose k}:e\cap [t-1]\ne\emptyset\right\\}\cup\left\\{[t+k]\setminus [t]\right\\}\cup\left\\{e\in {[n]\choose k}:e\cap [t]=\\{t\\},\\ e\cap ([t+k]\setminus [t])\ne\emptyset\right\\}.
$$

**Frankl–Kupavskii stability conjecture.** If $\nu(F)\le t$, then $\tau(F)\le t$ or

$$
e(F)\le\max\\{e({\cal A}_2^{(k)}(n,t)),\dots,e({\cal A}_k^{(k)}(n,t)),e({\cal H}^{(k)}(n,t))\\}.
$$

This is a stability strengthening of the Erdős Matching Conjecture, asserting that a $k$-graph with matching number at most $t$ either has a cover of size at most $t$ or is bounded by the extremal non-cover constructions. The supplied text gives no resolution status for this conjecture.
parsed_record.source_name: Hongliang Lu, Yan Wang and Xingxing Yu, “On stability of rainbow matchings”, arXiv:2302.06146 (2023).
parsed_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.06146

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2023).

parsed_record.title: Isometry classification conjecture for essential-rank-metric spaces
parsed_record.statement: Let $d53d$ be a field, let $S_{n,d}(d53d)$ denote the space of homogeneous degree-$d$ polynomials in $n$ variables, and let $\operatorname{d}_{\operatorname{ess}}$ be the essential-rank metric on this space. For $A\in\operatorname{GL}(n,d53d)$ and $\lambda\ind53d^*$, define the map $f\mapsto\lambda f\cdot A$, where $f\cdot A=f(x\cdot A)$. **Isometry classification conjecture.** Assume that $\operatorname{char}(d53d)=0$ or $\operatorname{char}(d53d)>d$. Then every isometry of $(S_{n,d}(d53d),\operatorname{d}_{\operatorname{ess}})$ is of the form $f\mapsto\lambda f\cdot A$ for some $A\in\operatorname{GL}(n,d53d)$ and $\lambda\ind53d^*$. The claim aims to classify all linear symmetries preserving essential rank; the preceding discussion establishes that maps of the displayed form are isometries, while the asserted converse remains conjectural under the stated characteristic condition.
parsed_record.source_name: Arthur Bik and Alessandro Neri, “Higher-degree symmetric rank-metric codes”, arXiv:2303.06745 (2023).

parsed_record.title: High-probability rank growth conjecture for generalized Moore matrices
parsed_record.statement:
Let $\bm{M} \in \mathbb{F}_{q^m}^{k \times n}$ be a randomly chosen matrix with full $\mathbb{F}_{q^m}$-rank such that each block $\bm{M}^{(i)}$, for $i=1,\dots,\ell$, has full column rank over $\mathbb{F}_q$. Let $\bm{a} \in \mathbb{F}_{q^m}^{\ell}$ consist of randomly chosen representatives of distinct nontrivial conjugacy classes of $\mathbb{F}_{q^m}$, and fix $j \in \{1,\dots,n-k\}$. **High-probability rank growth conjecture.** The iterated operator $\Gamma_{\bm{a}}^j$ satisfies

$$
\operatorname{rk}_{q^m}(\Gamma_{\bm{a}}^j(\bm{M}))=\min((j+1)k,n)
$$

with high probability. This claim is analogous to an assumption used for Overbeck's distinguisher and contrasts with the deterministic rank growth of generalized linearized Reed–Solomon codes; establishing the probability of this behavior for random full-rank matrices is the relevant issue.
parsed_record.source_name: Felicitas Hörmann, Hannes Bartz and Anna-Lena Horlemann, “Distinguishing and Recovering Generalized Linearized Reed-Solomon Codes”, arXiv:2304.00627 (2023).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.00627

parsed_record.title: The standard-orientation conjecture for interior polynomials of bipartite graphs
parsed_record.statement:
Let $\mathcal G$ be a bipartite graph with partite classes $U$ and $W$. A **standard orientation** is one in which every edge is oriented from $U$ to $W$, or every edge is oriented from $W$ to $U$; these two orientations have the same interior polynomial. A semi-balanced orientation is an orientation of $\mathcal G$ of the type considered in the source.

**Standard-orientation conjecture.** Among all semi-balanced orientations of a bipartite graph, the standard orientations minimize every coefficient of the interior polynomial.

The conjecture concerns how the interior polynomial varies with the orientation of a fixed bipartite graph. The source presents it as an open comparison problem; the two standard orientations are equivalent because their root polytopes are reflections of one another.
parsed_record.source_name: Tamás Kálmán and Lilla Tóthmérész, “Degrees of interior polynomials and parking function enumerators”, arXiv:2304.03221 (2025).
parsed_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.03221

Status: **open** according to the source (as of April 2023). “It remains an open problem which orientations minimize the degree of the interior polynomial among non-bipartite graphs.”

parsed_record.title: Panova's restricted #P conjecture for Kronecker coefficients
parsed_record.statement:
Let $\textsf{ComputeKron}$ be the problem of computing $g(\lambda,\mu,\nu)$ from partitions $\lambda,\mu,\nu$. Write $\ell(\lambda)$ for the number of parts of $\lambda$, and let $(n^d)$ denote the rectangular partition with $d$ parts equal to $n$.

**Panova's restricted-case conjecture.** The following two statements are each equivalent to the unrestricted assertion that $\textsf{ComputeKron}$ is in $\#\mathrm{P}$:

$$
\textsf{ComputeKron}\in\#\mathrm{P}\text{ when }\ell(\lambda)=2
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\textsf{ComputeKron}\in\#\mathrm{P},
$$

and

$$
\textsf{ComputeKron}\in\#\mathrm{P}\text{ for }\mu=\nu=(n^d),\ \lambda\vdash nd
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\textsf{ComputeKron}\in\#\mathrm{P}.
$$

These equivalences identify two restricted families whose membership in $\#\mathrm{P}$ would already settle the general counting question. The surrounding text presents this as a conjectural complexity statement about Kronecker coefficients.
parsed_record.source_name: Greta Panova, “Complexity and asymptotics of structure constants”, arXiv:2305.02553 (2023).
parsed_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.02553

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of May 2023).

parsed_record.title: The self-duality conjecture for finite LR-structures
parsed_record.statement:
Let $(\Gamma,\mathcal{C})$ be a finite LR-structure, and let $\operatorname{Aut}^+(\Gamma,\mathcal{C})$ denote its orientation-preserving automorphism group. The LR-structure is **self-dual** when an automorphism of $\Gamma$ interchanges its two distinguished sets of cycles, $\mathcal{L}$ and $\mathcal{R}$. **The self-duality conjecture.** If

$$
\operatorname{Aut}^+(\Gamma,\mathcal{C})<\operatorname{Aut}(\Gamma),
$$

then $(\Gamma,\mathcal{C})$ is self-dual. This conjecture asserts that, for a finite LR-structure, the equality of the lengths of the cycles in $\mathcal{L}$ and $\mathcal{R}$—known to be necessary for self-duality under this hypothesis—is also sufficient. The claim was posed as Conjecture 8.1 in the cited source; the material provided does not state whether it has been resolved.
parsed_record.source_name: Marston Conder, Luke Morgan and Primož Potočnik, “Resolution of a conjecture about linking ring structures”, arXiv:2305.04261 (2023).
parsed_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.04261

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2023).

parsed_record.title: Numerical Terao's conjecture for line arrangements
parsed_record.statement:
Let $\mathbb{F}$ be a fixed field and let $\mathcal{L} \subset \mathbb{P}^{2}_{\mathbb{F}}$ be an arrangement of $d$ lines. Its **weak-combinatorics** is the vector

$$
W(\mathcal{L})=(d;t_{2},\ldots,t_{d}),
$$

where $t_i$ denotes the number of $i$-fold intersection points, with zero entries for $i>m(\mathcal{L})$ omitted, where $m(\mathcal{L})$ is the maximal intersection multiplicity. A line arrangement is **free** when its associated derivation module is free.

**Numerical Terao's conjecture.** If $\mathcal{L}_{1},\mathcal{L}_{2}\subset\mathbb{P}^{2}_{\mathbb{F}}$ are line arrangements satisfying

$$
W(\mathcal{L}_{1})=W(\mathcal{L}_{2}),
$$

then $\mathcal{L}_{1}$ is free if and only if $\mathcal{L}_{2}$ is free.

This asks whether freeness can be determined by the numerical data of intersection points, which is weaker than the full intersection lattice. The source presents it as a weaker version of Terao's conjecture; no resolution is given.
parsed_record.source_name: Lukas Kühne, Dante Luber and Piotr Pokora, “On the numerical Terao's conjecture and Ziegler pairs for line arrangements”, arXiv:2407.07070 (2025).
parsed_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.07070

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2024).

parsed_record.title: Lew's extremal characterization conjecture for simplicial complexes
parsed_record.statement:
Let $X$ be a simplicial complex on vertex set $V$ of size $n$, with $h(X)=d$. Write $\mu_k(X)$ for the parameter appearing in the equality below, and let $\Delta_m$ denote the complete simplicial complex on $m+1$ vertices; $\Delta_d^{(d-1)}$ is its $(d-1)$-dimensional skeleton. The symbol $*$ denotes the join of simplicial complexes, and $X\cong Y$ means that $X$ and $Y$ are isomorphic simplicial complexes. **Lew's conjecture.** If

$$
\mu_k(X)=(d+1)(k+1)-dn
$$

for some $k$, then

$$
X\cong \left(\Delta_d^{(d-1)}\right)^{*(n-k-1)}*\Delta_{(d+1)(k+1)-dn-1}.
$$

In particular, $\dim(X)=k$. Lew proposed this as a characterization of the simplicial complexes attaining equality in the relevant spectral-gap lower bound; the supplied source does not state whether the conjecture has been resolved.
parsed_record.source_name: Xiongfeng Zhan, Xueyi Huang and Huiqiu Lin, “Proof of Lew's conjecture on the spectral gaps of simplicial complexes”, arXiv:2407.10398 (2024).
parsed_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.10398

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2024).

parsed_record.title: Hazrat's shift-equivalence conjecture for Cuntz–Krieger and Leavitt path algebras
parsed_record.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be two finite **essential matrices**, and let $A$ and $B$ be **shift equivalent** (SE) when they are shift equivalent as nonnegative integer matrices. Denote by $\mathcal{O}_A$ and $\mathcal{O}_B$ the Cuntz–Krieger graph C*-algebras, with canonical gauge actions $\gamma^A$ and $\gamma^B$, and by $L_A$ and $L_B$ the associated Leavitt path algebras. The algebras $L_A$ and $L_B$ are **graded Morita equivalent** when they are Morita equivalent through equivalences preserving the grading.

**Hazrat's conjecture.** The following are equivalent:

1. $A$ and $B$ are SE.
2. $\mathcal{O}_A$ and $\mathcal{O}_B$ are stably isomorphic in a way preserving their gauge actions $\gamma^A$ and $\gamma^B$.
3. $L_A$ and $L_B$ are graded Morita equivalent.

This conjecture seeks a converse to Krieger's result that gauge-action-preserving stable isomorphism of the Cuntz–Krieger graph C*-algebras implies shift equivalence, while also asserting the corresponding equivalence with graded Morita equivalence of Leavitt path algebras. The supplied text does not state whether the conjecture has been resolved.
parsed_record.source_name: Boris Bilich, Adam Dor-On and Efren Ruiz, “Equivariant homotopy classification of graph C*-algebras”, arXiv:2408.09740 (2024).
parsed_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.09740

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2024).

parsed_record.title: Bachmann's conjecture on relations among Schlesinger–Zudilin $q$-multiple zeta values
parsed_record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{U}$ be the alphabet used to form the noncommutative word algebra $\mathbb{Q}\langle\mathcal{U}\rangle$, let $\mathbb{Q}\langle\mathcal{U}\rangle^\circ$ be the subspace spanned by words not starting with $u_0$, and let

$$
\zeta_q^\mathrm{SZ}\colon \mathbb{Q}\langle\mathcal{U}\rangle^\circ\to\mathbb{Q}\llbracket q\rrbracket
$$

be the Schlesinger–Zudilin $q$-multiple-zeta-value map, with image $\mathcal{Z}_q$. The algebra carries the **stuffle product** $\ast$, and it has the involution **duality** $\tau$ defined on words by

$$
\tau\left(u_{k_1}u_0^{z_1}\cdots u_{k_d}u_0^{z_d}\right)=u_{z_d+1}u_0^{k_d-1}\cdots u_{z_1+1}u_0^{k_1-1}.
$$

**Bachmann's conjecture.** All $\mathbb{Q}$-linear relations among elements of $\mathcal{Z}_q$ are generated by the stuffle product $\ast$ and duality $\tau$. This conjecturally gives a complete description of the linear relations among Schlesinger–Zudilin $q$-multiple zeta values, while the general completeness of these two families of relations remains open.
parsed_record.source_name: Benjamin Brindle, “Combinatorial interpretation of the Schlesinger-Zudilin stuffle product”, arXiv:2409.16966 (2025).
parsed_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.16966

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2024).

parsed_record.title: Uniqueness conjecture for the toroidal penny graph embedding of $K_{3,3}$
parsed_record.statement:
A **toroidal penny graph** is a contact graph of congruent non-overlapping disks embedded on a flat torus, with vertices representing disk centers and edges representing tangent pairs. Consider the embedding of $K_{3,3}$ whose toroidal coordinates are given by

$$
\left(\frac{13}{36},-\frac{13}{36}\right),
\left(\frac{11}{36},\frac{1}{36}\right),
\left(\frac{1}{36},\frac{11}{36}\right),
\left(-\frac{13}{36},\frac{13}{36}\right),
\left(-\frac{11}{36},-\frac{1}{36}\right),
\left(-\frac{1}{36},-\frac{11}{36}\right).
$$

**Uniqueness conjecture for the $K_{3,3}$ embedding.** The proposed embedding of $K_{3,3}$, with coordinates as described in the table, is unique up to an isometry.

The claim concerns the rigidity of the exhibited toroidal penny graph realization of $K_{3,3}$: no non-isometric embedding with the same graph is expected to exist. The source provides the embedding and its packing radius but gives no resolution of this uniqueness question.
parsed_record.source_name: Cédric Lorand, “K5 and K3,3 are Toroidal Penny Graphs”, arXiv:2410.10673 (2024).

parsed_record.title: Tropicalization conjecture for the type C cluster configuration space
parsed_record.statement:
Let $N$ be the label set for the binary geometry defining the type C cluster configuration space, and let $\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{C}_{n-1}}$ be its very affine part in $u$-coordinates. An **axially symmetric phylogenetic tree** (ASPT) is an axially symmetric tree with $2n$ labeled leaves, and for each ASPT $(T,\varphi)$ let $C_{T,\varphi}$ denote the associated cone.

**Tropicalization conjecture.** The tropicalization $\operatorname{Trop}\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{C}_{n-1}}$ is the space of ASPTs: the fan formed by the cones $C_{T,\varphi}$ with $(T,\varphi)$ ranging over all ASPTs.

This conjecture proposes a combinatorial description of the tropicalization of the type C cluster configuration space, identifying its fan structure with the complex of axially symmetric phylogenetic trees. The source presents this as the first conjecture; no resolution status is supplied.

parsed_record.title: Partial-fraction decomposition conjecture for flat-space wavefunctions
parsed_record.statement:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a Feynman graph with $n$ vertices. Let $\mathcal{F}=\{H_1,H_2,\dots,H_r\}$ be the set of spanning subgraphs of $G$, including their orientations, and write $H_i^1,\ldots,H_i^{s_i}$ for the connected components of $H_i$. For a connected oriented subgraph $H$, let $R_H(X,Y)$ be the rational function defined from the linear forms $\ell(H)$ and the admissible positive-degree connected subgraphs, with $R_H(X,Y)=0$ when $H$ contains a directed cycle.

**Flat-space partial-fraction decomposition conjecture.** The flat-space wavefunction can be decomposed into partial fractions as

$$
\psi_{\text{flat}}=\sum_{H_i\in\mathcal{F}}(-1)^{n-1-|E(H_i)|}\prod_{j=1}^{s_i}R_{H_i^j}(X,Y).
$$

This claim gives a graph-theoretic partial-fraction formula for the flat-space wavefunction. The source presents it as a conjecture but supplies no evidence of resolution in the provided text, so it remains open.
parsed_record.source_name: Claudia Fevola, Guilherme L. Pimentel, Anna-Laura Sattelberger and Tom Westerdijk, “Algebraic Approaches to Cosmological Integrals”, arXiv:2410.14757 (2025).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.14757

parsed_record.title: The cut-partition characterization of fullerenes without generalized Stone–Wales paths
parsed_record.statement:
Let $T_n$ be a dual fullerene graph and let $T_n^6$ be its hexagonal subgraph, for feasible $n$. A **cut-partition** of $T_n^6$ is the set of components generated by the stated cut-partition construction; $t$-triangles and $(t,(r_1,r_2,r_3))$-triangles are the triangle types defined there, and a **gSW path** is a generalized Stone–Wales path. **Cut-partition characterization conjecture.** The cut-partition of $T_n^6$ consists solely of elements that are either $t$-triangles or $(t,(r_1,r_2,r_3))$-triangles if and only if $T_n$ contains no gSW path, with the exception that the cut-partition contains only $0$-triangles.

This conjecture proposes a structural characterization of the absence of generalized Stone–Wales paths using the cut-partition. It is presented as a numerical conjecture, with no resolution stated in the source.
parsed_record.source_name: Artur Bille, Victor Buchstaber and Evgeny Spodarev, “Some open mathematical problems on fullerenes”, arXiv:2410.19322 (2024).

parsed_record.title: Laplacian zero-eigenvalue multiplicity conjecture for connected uniform hypergraphs
parsed_record.statement:
Let $H$ be a connected $k$-uniform hypergraph, let $\mathcal{L}(H)$ be its Laplacian tensor, let $\mathcal{A}(H)$ be its adjacency tensor, and let $rho$ be the spectral radius of $\mathcal{A}(H)$. Write $\mathrm{am}(0,\mathcal{L}(H))$ and $\mathrm{am}(rho,\mathcal{A}(H))$ for the corresponding algebraic multiplicities, and let $\mathbb{V}_0(\mathcal{L}(H))$ denote the projective eigenvariety for the zero eigenvalue. **Laplacian zero-eigenvalue multiplicity conjecture.**

$$
\mathrm{am}(0,\mathcal{L}(H))=\mathrm{am}(rho,\mathcal{A}(H)),
$$

and consequently

$$
\mathrm{am}(0,\mathcal{L}(H))=|\mathbb{V}_0(\mathcal{L}(H))|.
$$

The first equality is established in the paper for $k$-uniform hypertrees, and the authors propose its extension to all connected $k$-uniform hypergraphs; the consequence then follows from the relation between the corresponding projective eigenvarieties.
parsed_record.source_name: Yi-Zheng Fan, “The multiplicity of eigenvalues of nonnegative weakly irreducible tensors and uniform hypergraphs”, arXiv:2410.20830 (2024).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.20830

parsed_record.title: The characterization of graphs with tree reconfiguration graphs
parsed_record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, and let $\mathcal{R}(G)$ denote its reconfiguration graph. Here, $\mathcal{R}(G)$ is the graph whose vertices represent minimal domination sets of $G$, with adjacency given by the reconfiguration relation defined in the paper. Let $\overline{K_n}$ be the edgeless graph on $n$ vertices, let $K_{1,m}$ be the star with $m$ leaves, and let $\cup$ denote disjoint union.

**Tree reconfiguration graph conjecture.** $\mathcal{R}(G)$ is a tree if and only if

$$
G \cong \overline{K_n} \cup K_{1,m}
$$

for some non-negative integers $m$ and $n$.

The conjecture seeks a complete characterization of graphs whose minimal-domination-set reconfiguration graph is a tree. The paper establishes several related connectivity and characterization results, but the stated equivalence is presented as a conjecture.
parsed_record.source_name: Iain Beaton, “Reconfiguration graphs for minimal domination sets”, arXiv:2411.02300 (2024).

parsed_record.title: Tight Bayesian optimal uniform reserve approximation for quasi-regular buyers
parsed_record.statement:
Let asymmetric and symmetric buyers have quasi-regular valuation distributions, and let $\calC_{{\sf BOM}}^{\textsf{Bayesian Optimal Uniform Reserve}}$ denote the revenue approximation ratio of **Bayesian Optimal Uniform Reserve** to **Bayesian Optimal Mechanism**. **Bayesian Optimal Uniform Reserve conjecture.** For asymmetric quasi-regular buyers, the tight ratio equals the regular-buyer bound

$$
\calC_{{\sf BOM}}^{\textsf{Bayesian Optimal Uniform Reserve}}\in[0.3817,0.4630],
$$

while for symmetric quasi-regular buyers it equals

$$
\calC_{{\sf BOM}}^{\textsf{Bayesian Optimal Uniform Reserve}}=1+\left(W_{-1}\left(-\frac{1}{e^2}\right)\right)^{-1}\approx0.6822.
$$

The conjecture would extend the known asymmetric regular-buyer bounds to asymmetric quasi-regular buyers and identify the symmetric quasi-regular worst case; the proposed reduction from quasi-regular to regular buyers remains to be established.
parsed_record.source_name: Yiding Feng and Yaonan Jin, “Beyond Regularity: Simple versus Optimal Mechanisms, Revisited”, arXiv:2411.03583 (2024).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.03583

Status: **open** according to the source (as of November 2024).

parsed_record.title: Lower-bound conjecture for the effective squeezing parameter
parsed_record.statement:
Let $\rho$ be a physical state on an $n$-mode quantum system with average photon number

$$
\overline{N}=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho\hat{N}).
$$

For a symplectic basis $M=(\bs{\xi}_1,\hdots,\bs{\xi}_{2n})^T$, define the effective squeezing parameter by

$$
\tilde{\Delta}^2(\rho)\coloneqq \min_{M\in\operatorname{Sp}_{2n}(\mathbb{R})}\min_i\Delta^2_{\bs{\xi}_i}(\rho).
$$

**Effective-squeezing lower-bound conjecture.** The effective squeezing satisfies

$$
\tilde{\Delta}^2(\rho)\geq \frac{4}{\overline{N}}.
$$

The conjecture would give a lower bound depending only on the state's average photon number, supporting the physicality assumptions used to control local GKP shadow sample complexity. The supplied text motivates the bound from approximate GKP states but does not establish it for general physical states.
parsed_record.source_name: Jonathan Conrad, Joseph T. Iosue, Ansgar G. Burchards and Victor V. Albert, “Continuous-variable designs and design-based shadow tomography from random lattices”, arXiv:2412.17909 (2025).
parsed_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.17909

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2024).
